metaDescription: Six 45 pint dehumidifiers compared on stated test conditions, noise, drain hose length and coverage for large basements and whole-floor use.
expertTake: The ASAHWo Energy Star unit with a 44 dB low speed is the pick for most large homes. The Trazico is the value pick because it ships a long hose. Skip a 45 pint machine if your damp area is a single closet or bathroom, since it will short-cycle and waste power.
introParagraphs: A 45 pint dehumidifier is built for floors, not rooms: a full basement, a big open lower level or a house that runs humid through the summer. At this size the compressor, the fan and the drain setup all matter more than they do on a small unit.

The catch is the label. Many sellers print a pint figure taken at a hot, saturated test point, so two machines that look identical on paper can behave very differently once the room is cool. This guide reads the fine print so you do not have to.

products.name: ASAHWo 45 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier 4,500 sq ft
products.description:
This ASAHWo is a compressor unit sized for a large lower level, and it carries an Energy Star Most Efficient designation on the listing. The lowest fan speed is quoted at 44 dB, which the seller compares to white noise, and the electronics adjust output automatically to the humidity they sense. For a machine that may run most of the day, those two traits matter more than any marketing pint figure.

The tradeoff is that you are buying a large, heavy appliance with a newer brand name. Against the other ASAHWo model in this guide, it trades a few features for a lower noise claim. Against the Tehanld, it gives up the larger rating and tank, and gains efficiency and quieter operation.

Ownership is routine: wash the filter, wipe the tank and give the unit 6 to 12 inches of clearance. Because the efficient compressor runs for long stretches, a hygrometer in the room tells you whether the target is actually being held. The 44 dB figure refers to the lowest fan speed, so expect more noise when it ramps up after a wet day. In year three the realistic wear points are the fan bearing and the float switch.
products.bestFor: Large finished or semi-finished lower levels where noise and running cost matter.
pros: 44 dB lowest speed suits living areas
Covers up to 4,500 sq ft by the claim
cons: Newer brand with a short service record
Large and heavy to move for cleaning

products.name: Trazico 45 Pint Dehumidifier 4,000 sq ft with 4.9 ft Hose
products.description:
The Trazico is a plain, honest 45 pint compressor unit with a 4.9 foot drain hose in the box. That hose length is nearly half again as long as the short hoses on many competitors, which gives you more freedom to place it away from the drain. Continuous drainage means you can leave it running unattended.

It has a DEHU mode for everyday control and a DRY mode aimed at laundry on rainy days. In the price tier it sits low among the 45 pint units, which makes it the sensible pick when you want the size without paying for extras. It does not list the noise figure of the ASAHWo, so assume a normal compressor hum.

Owners should plan on routine filter washes and a hose check each season. Slope the hose downhill and keep it free of kinks so the tank never has to carry the load. Compared with the ASAHWo, you give up the efficiency badge but keep the size and save in price tier. A long hose also helps when the drain sits across the room.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a true 45 pint size and a long drain hose at a low price tier.
pros: 4.9 ft hose included for flexible placement
Low price tier for the size

products.name: ASAHWo 45 Pint Dehumidifier 4,500 sq ft with 24H Timer
products.description:
This second ASAHWo is honest about its test: 45 pints at 95F and 90 percent humidity. That is a hot, saturated point, so a cool basement will yield less, but it is a useful reminder to read the condition on every listing. The target range runs from 30 to 80 percent, which gives wide control.

The 24 hour timer lets you run the machine only when you want, and the automatic defrost keeps the coil from icing in cooler rooms. Three modes cover everyday control, laundry and continuous use. It sits higher in price tier than the Trazico, mainly for the scheduling and defrost.

Use the timer to run it in the warmest part of the day, when the compressor is most efficient. Clean the filter on schedule and verify humidity with a separate meter. If the basement stays near 60F, the defrost cycles will lengthen run time, so leave room for it to catch up before judging output.
products.bestFor: Cool basements and homes where scheduling and defrost control help.
pros: Stated test condition on the listing
cons: Rating is taken at 95F and 90% RH
Higher price tier than the Trazico

products.name: MIONJO 45-80 Pint Dehumidifier 4,500 sq ft with Hose
products.description:
MIONJO quotes a capacity range of 45 to 80 pints, which tells you the 45 figure is the conservative end and 80 is the hot-lab number. The 90 degree adjustable outlet lets you aim dry air into a corner or along a wall, which helps in oddly shaped basements. The seller quotes 40 dB, among the quietest claims here.

The flip side is the same as with any range: you should plan around the lower number. Compared with the ASAHWo, it adds the aimable outlet and a lower noise claim, and lands in a higher price tier. Energy Star status keeps running cost in check.

Aim the outlet away from furniture and keep it clear of curtains. Filter and tank upkeep follow the usual schedule. Because it lists a range instead of one figure, ask what you would do if it delivered the low end, and size accordingly.
products.bestFor: Irregular basements where aiming the airflow helps.
pros: 40 dB noise claim is among the lowest
cons: Capacity range is wide and vague

products.name: DGVAM 45-80 Pint Energy Star Dehumidifier 4,500 sq ft
products.description:
DGVAM sells a similar spec sheet to the MIONJO: 45 to 80 pints, 4,500 square feet and Energy Star certification. Smart sensors track humidity and adjust output automatically to hold a balanced level. It ships with a drain hose for continuous operation.

It lacks a published noise figure, so compare it by price tier and warranty, not by quiet. Against the Trazico, you get a larger coverage claim and Energy Star status, at a mid-tier price.

As with all the 45 to 80 range models, plan for the lower pint number and keep the filter and coil clean. The smart sensors save effort, but a separate hygrometer is still worth a few dollars of cost to check them.
products.bestFor: Large open spaces where smart auto control and Energy Star matter.

products.name: Tehanld 50 Pint Dehumidifier 5,000 sq ft with Hose
products.description:
If 45 pints feels borderline, the Tehanld steps up to a 50 pint rating and a 5,000 square foot claim. A heavy-duty compressor does the work, and the 1.6 gallon removable tank has auto shutoff with an indicator light. That tank is among the largest in the lineup.

It offers a humidity range of 30 to 80 percent, a laundry mode and a hose option for continuous drain. Compared with the ASAHWo, it is rated higher but does not list an efficiency badge.

Register the warranty and keep the tank handle clean. The unit is heavy when full, so use both hands. Its larger compressor also warms the room a few degrees, which helps in a cool cellar but not in a bedroom.
products.bestFor: Very damp or large spaces where a 45 pint unit might run flat out.
cons: Heavy when the tank is full

buyingCriteria.explanation: The ASAHWo B0HDP1SJLK states 45 pints at 95F and 90 percent humidity, a hot test point. The 2019 US test is 65F and 60 percent, which gives lower numbers. A 45 pint label at 95F is closer to a 30 pint machine at 65F, so the same number can mean very different output. Always ask what the number would be at 65F before you compare two labels.

The MIONJO and DGVAM list 45 to 80 pints. The low number is the one to plan around, and 80 is a lab peak. If a listing gives a range, treat the bottom as the real figure. Treat 80 as marketing and plan on 45.

The Trazico ships a 4.9 foot hose, longer than many competitors. A short hose forces the machine next to the drain, which may not be where the damp air sits. Measure the run before you buy. Measure the distance from the machine to the drain before choosing.

At 44 dB, the ASAHWo is close to a quiet room. The MIONJO claims 40 dB. A 10 dB difference sounds about twice as loud, so a living space deserves a published low figure. Check the low-speed figure, not the high.

Compressor units lose output below about 65F and need defrost cycles. The ASAHWo with the timer lists automatic defrost. A cold cellar needs a unit with margin, such as the 50 pint Tehanld. A cold cellar needs margin, not just a badge.

A machine this size draws roughly 500 to 800 watts. The ASAHWo Energy Star Most Efficient label and the MIONJO and DGVAM Energy Star status point to lower use per pint. Over a season, that offsets a modest price gap. Efficiency compounds over months of running.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each listing states its test condition or a range. The ASAHWo with the timer named 95F and 90% RH. Ranges like 45 to 80 pints were treated as 45. That makes the list a ranking of honesty first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hose length, tank size and shutoff. The Trazico's 4.9 ft hose and the Tehanld's 1.6 gallon tank stood out. Tank size matters most when you skip the hose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We read decibel claims. The MIONJO at 40 dB and the ASAHWo at 44 dB led. Quiet matters most for sleeping areas.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed Energy Star status. The ASAHWo Most Efficient label scored highest. Running cost is a long-term factor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at filters, defrost and owner feedback patterns on durability for newer brands. Warranty and service reach round out the picture.

cards.label: Fixed rating
cards.text: Trazico and Tehanld give one number. It is easier to compare and plan around.

cards.label: Range
cards.text: MIONJO and DGVAM list 45 to 80 pints, hiding the realistic figure behind a hot-lab peak.

howToChoose.note: Pick a fixed rating unless the other specs win it for you.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Whole Lower Level Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Real capacity at 65F, a long hose or a pump route and a quiet low speed. Place it in the middle of the space.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ASAHWo 45 Pint is the best all-round fit. The Tehanld handles a worse problem.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You will run it every day. The ASAHWo efficiency and the MIONJO noise repay a premium.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The space is a seasonal basement. The Trazico covers it.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter reduces airflow and frosts the coil.
Kinks and algae slow flow and cause overflow.

faq.q: Is a 45 pint unit better than a 35 pint?
faq.a: It is better for larger areas, and only if the test conditions match. Compare the stated temperature and humidity on each label. Look at coverage in square feet only after the rating.

faq.q: How much does a 45 pint dehumidifier cost?
faq.a: Prices run from a low tier to a premium tier. Check the listing since prices move. Warranty terms differ between brands, so read them.
Only if the drain is above the unit. Otherwise a gravity hose works. A clean filter and coil add years.
Compressor units typically last 5 to 10 years. Keeping the filter and coil clean helps. Hot-lab ratings overstate cool-room output.

faq.q: What does a capacity range mean?
faq.a: A range like 45 to 80 pints gives a realistic low and a hot-lab high. Plan around the low number. Hold the target on cool nights too.
Aim for 40 to 50 percent. Above 60 percent encourages mold. A separate meter costs little.
